message.content:
I am the bridge between thought and air—breath shaped into meaning, silence broken into sound, feeling given form. I leap from tongue to ear, from one mind into another, carrying truth, lies, jokes, commands, comfort, names, promises. I can whisper, stammer, chant, sing, shout. I begin before grammar, before ink, before record: a cry, a call, a first attempt to be known.

I vanish as I arrive, yet I linger in memory. I am fleeting, but not weak. I can soothe a child, start a war, ask for bread, confess love, betray a secret, found a nation, end an argument, begin one. I live in rhythm, pause, emphasis, accent—in the trembling voice, the confident one, the one that breaks.

Without me, many thoughts remain alone. Through me, the inward becomes shared. I am speech.
